runs.text: A nested loop is a loop inside another loop. Multiple loops can be placed inside one loop, and this can continue to more than one level.
2. What are jump statements? Name them.
Jump statements change the normal flow of execution by moving the control from one place to another. The statements covered here are break, continue and return.
3. What does the return statement do inside a loop? Giv

return sends the control back to the place from where it came. In the main method, the control came from the JVM, so as soon as return executes, the control goes back to the JVM and the program ends. The loop below could run more than once, b
ut the statement after the print is return, so the message is printed only once.
4. What does the break statement do, and where can it be used?

blocks.text: break brings the control out of the construct in which it is placed, and the execution continues with the statement after that construct. break can be used only inside loops (for, while, do-while) and inside a switch. Using it anywhere else is a compile-time error.

runs.text: 5. What is the output of the following program?
The control enters the loop, prints Hello, and break immediately takes the control out of the loop. The statement after the loop then prints World. The loop does not run again.

7. What is the difference between break and continue?

blocks.text: break brings the control out of the loop (or switch) in which it is placed. continue does not leave the loop; it takes the control back to the loop to start the next iteration without executing the remaining statements. break can be used in loops and switch, while continue is used in loops.

runs.text: 8. What is the output of the following nested loop program?
The outer loop repeats 3 times. In every iteration it prints Hello, then the inner loop prints World twice
, and then How are you is printed. So the group Hello, World, World, How are you is repeated three times.

A label means a name. Analogy: when someone is called a bad name in front of others, that person has been labeled. In the same way, you can give a name to a loop by writing the name and a colon before the loop. The label can then be used with break or cont
inue to say exactly which loop the statement should apply to.

runs.text: 13. Can a label be used with continue?
Yes. Labels can be used with both break and continue. continue followed by the label of the outer loop skips the rest of the current iteration of the inner l

oop and also the rest of the outer loop body, and moves the control to the next iteration of the labeled outer loop. In short: break label ends the labeled loop, and continue label goes on to the next iteration of the labeled loop.
